title: "Decision Boundary"
description: "The surface separating regions assigned to different classes by a classifier."
term: "Decision Boundary"
letter: "D"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

A decision boundary is the line, curve, or higher-dimensional surface
that separates the regions where a classifier predicts different classes.

## Technical explanation

For a classifier with decision function $f(x)$, a binary decision boundary
often consists of points where class scores are equal or where
$f(x)=0$. Its shape depends on the model, features, parameters, and
decision threshold. In high-dimensional settings the boundary cannot
usually be visualized directly.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The boundary helps explain how a model separates classes and how
predictions may change near uncertain regions. It can inform feature
analysis, threshold selection, and targeted data collection.

## How it works

The model maps an input to scores or probabilities. A decision rule assigns
a class according to those outputs. The set of inputs where the assigned
class changes forms the decision boundary.

## Practical example

For a two-feature classifier, plotting the two features and coloring each
region by the predicted class can reveal whether the model uses a straight
line or a more complex boundary.

## Common misconceptions

- A visually simple boundary in a two-dimensional plot may not describe
  behaviour across all features.
- A point near the boundary is not necessarily equally likely to belong to
  either class unless the model is appropriately calibrated.
- Changing the classification threshold can move the boundary without
  changing the underlying model parameters.
